subject: general
question: A policeman spotted a thief at a distance of 1,500 metres and he immediately started chasing him at 20 km/h. The thief spotted the policeman at the same time and immediately started running away from him at 15 km/h. How far will the thief run before he gets caught?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.

Ratio of Speeds (Police : Thief) = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3.

Ratio of Distances = 4 : 3 → Difference = 1 unit.

Given 1 unit = 1,500 m ∴ Thief distance = 3 units = 3 × 1,500 m.

**∴ Answer = 4,500 metres**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between Police and Thief = 1,500 m

Speed of Police = 20 km/h | Speed of Thief = 15 km/h

**Formula used:**

Relative Speed = Speed₁ − Speed₂ (same direction)

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed | Distance = Speed × Time

 Police (P) 20 km/h Thief (T) 15 km/h Catch Point 
• 1500 m 
• Distance = 4500 m Relative Speed = 5 km/h 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed of Police with respect to Thief = 20 − 15 = 5 km/h

⇒ Since time taken by both to meet is the same, we use the ratio of their speeds.

⇒ Ratio of Distance (P : T) = Speed Ratio (P : T) = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3

⇒ Difference in distance units = 4 − 3 = 1 unit

⇒ 1 unit = 1,500 m

⇒ Distance covered by Thief before being caught = 3 units = 3 × 1,500 m

⇒ Distance = 4,500 m

**∴ The correct answer is 4,500 metres (Option 4).**
